question: Assume today is 2026-09-05. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the number of new passenger cars (Pkw) registered in Germany in September 2026, as it will be first reported in the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt's (KBA) monthly press release on vehicle registrations.

target.what: Number of new passenger cars (Pkw) with first registration in Germany during September 2026, as reported by the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt (KBA) in its monthly press release on vehicle registrations (Fahrzeugzulassungen). Counts new Pkw first registrations (Neuzulassungen), including passenger cars of dom
target.cadence: monthly press release, typically published in the first week of the following month
target.caveats: Target period is future relative to the 2026-09-05 cutoff, so no September 2026 data exist yet; estimate must be built from prior-year September levels, 2026 YTD momentum, calendar effects (September 2026 has 22 working days; no major holiday distortions), and known policy/EV incentive changes. Alte

candidates.hypothesis: September new Pkw registrations in prior years (2019, 2023, 2024, 2025) plus the 2026 monthly YTD series establish a base level and seasonal September factor; September is typically a strong month (post-summer, pre-Q4), so September 2026 ≈ recent monthly run-rate × September seasonal index.
candidates.data_to_find: KBA monthly new Pkw registrations for September 2019, 2023, 2024, 2025 and monthly values Jan–Aug 2026 (or latest available before cutoff); also September seasonal index (Sep/avg-month ratio) over 2015–2025.

candidates.perspective: European auto market (ACEA) and German passenger car market
candidates.hypothesis: Germany's share of EU new car registrations is stable (~20–22%); ACEA monthly EU totals and Germany's share can cross-check the KBA-derived level and flag whether 2026 German demand is running above/below the EU trend.
candidates.data_to_find: ACEA monthly new passenger car registrations for EU and Germany, Jan–Aug 2026 and September 2025; Germany share of EU total.
search_hints: ACEA passenger car registrations September 2025 Germany

candidates.hypothesis: VDA, ifo, and analyst forecasts for 2026 German passenger car registrations (full-year) can be divided into months using seasonal weights to bound September 2026; a full-year forecast of ~2.8–2.9 million implies ~230–260k in September.
candidates.data_to_find: Full-year 2026 German new Pkw registration forecasts from VDA, ifo, Bloomberg/Reuters consensus, or OEM guidance as of mid-2026; any monthly guidance.

candidates.hypothesis: Changes to EV purchase incentives (Umweltbonus ended 2023; possible 2025–2026 reintroduction or company-car tax changes) and CO2/fleet rules shift September 2026 registrations via pull-forward or payback effects; a known incentive change effective Q4 2026 could pull registrations into September.
candidates.data_to_find: German government EV/plug-in incentive status and any announced changes effective 2026; company car benefit tax (Dienstwagensteuer) changes; EU CO2 fleet targets 2025–2027 phase-in effects on registration timing.

candidates.hypothesis: German OEM domestic production plus imports minus exports approximates available supply; if production is constrained (chip/energy) or inventories are high, registrations deviate from demand. September registrations ≈ dealer deliveries, which track production ~4–8 weeks earlier.
candidates.data_to_find: German passenger car production (Inlandsproduktion) and export/import volumes for July–August 2026 (VDA/Statistisches Bundesamt); dealer inventory or days-supply indicators.

candidates.hypothesis: Monthly registrations scale with selling days; September 2026 has 22 working days vs August's ~21, and September historically runs ~10–15% above the annual monthly average; a day-adjusted run-rate from July–August 2026 gives a September anchor.
candidates.data_to_find: Working/selling days per month in Germany 2026; historical ratio of September registrations to July–August average (2015–2025).

candidates.hypothesis: BEV/PHEV share shifts affect total volume because incentive-driven BEV demand can add or subtract registrations; splitting September 2026 into ICE + BEV + PHEV using recent shares and known policy gives a cross-check on the aggregate.
candidates.data_to_find: KBA monthly new Pkw registrations by fuel type (BEV, PHEV, petrol, diesel) Jan–Aug 2026 and September 2025; BEV share trend.

assumptions.applies_when: No 2026 monthly YTD series or policy shock is available to adjust the September 2025 base.
assumptions.falsified_by: A 2026 YTD series showing strong growth or decline, or a known Q4 2026 incentive change pulling registrations into September.

assumptions.name: September seasonal index vs annual monthly average

assumptions.applies_when: A full-year 2026 forecast is available and must be distributed to September.
assumptions.falsified_by: A September seasonal factor materially outside 1.05-1.20 in recent KBA data.

final.template:
The best computed estimate for new passenger car (Pkw) first registrations in Germany during September 2026, as to be reported by the KBA, is [[estimate]] [[unit]] ([[interval_level]] interval [[p10]] to [[p90]] [[unit]]). This combines [[n_methods]] methods at equal weight ([[m1_weight]] and [[m2_weight]]).

The only observed anchor is September 2025 at [[p1_value]]. Method m1 ([[m1_estimate]] [[unit]]) applies a YoY change factor of [[a1_value]] (range [[a1_low]] to [[a1_high]]) to that base. Method m2 ([[m2_estimate]] [[unit]]) scales the same base by a September seasonal index of [[a2_value]] (range [[a2_low]] to [[a2_high]]). Both routes therefore rest entirely on the single observed point; the YoY factor and seasonal index are analyst assumptions, not observations. Equal weighting reflects the absence of backtest evidence to favor either.

The main risk is a large 2026 market shift (policy or EV-incentive effects) not captured by the flat carry. The most useful missing evidence is the 2026 year-to-date KBA monthly series, which would replace the assumed momentum with observed data.

Key assumptions (proposed by the analyst model, not observed; code samples each one between the bounds shown):
- a1 September 2026 YoY change factor vs September 2025: [[a1_value]] dimensionless, range [[a1_low]] to [[a1_high]]; used by m1. Overturned by: A 2026 YTD series showing a sharp market contraction or boom, or a known Q4 2026 incentive change pulling registrations into September.
- a2 September seasonal index vs annual monthly average: [[a2_value]] dimensionless, range [[a2_low]] to [[a2_high]] (range widened by code); used by m2. Overturned by: Evidence of an unusual September calendar or a policy deadline shifting registrations out of the month.

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
